Food.title: Food Log

categoryHelp.vegetable: Vegetables of all kinds: zucchini, pumpkin, potato, carrot, broccoli, etc., well cooked and without salt.
categoryHelp.fruit: Fresh and ripe fruits (banana, pear, apple, peach, citrus...), preferably whole or in pieces/puree rather than juice.
categoryHelp.grain: Cereals and starches: rice, oats, bread, pasta, corn, potato, sweet potato, quinoa... prioritizing whole grains and no added sugar.
categoryHelp.animal_protein: Meat (chicken, turkey, beef, pork), fish, seafood, egg, organ meats in small amounts.
categoryHelp.plant_protein: Legumes (lentils, chickpeas, beans, soy) and derivatives like tofu; nuts and seeds always ground or in cream, never whole.
categoryHelp.dairy: For <12 months: main milk is breast milk or formula; other dairy (yogurt, cheese) in small amounts. After 1 year, whole milk, yogurt, and cheese.
categoryHelp.other: Healthy fats (olive oil, avocado) and occasional foods (avoid sugar and processed foods).

ForbiddenFoods.title: Foods to avoid or delay
ForbiddenFoods.milk: Whole cow's milk as a main drink (small amounts of yogurt or cheese are allowed from ~9–10 months, depending on tolerance).
ForbiddenFoods.salt: Do not add salt to meals due to renal immaturity; at most a pinch of iodized salt near the first year.
ForbiddenFoods.sugar: Added sugar, honey, juices, pastries, cookies, sugary cereals, and other superfluous products.
ForbiddenFoods.choking: Whole nuts, peanuts, whole grapes, sliced sausages, olives, hard candies, and other round/hard foods.
ForbiddenFoods.chokingAdvice: Offer crushed, ground, or cut lengthwise, depending on age.
ForbiddenFoods.mercury: Large fish with high mercury content (bluefin tuna, swordfish/emperor, pike) should be avoided in children under 3 years.

AllergenicFoods.title: High Allergy Risk Foods
AllergenicFoods.description: The foods with the highest allergy risk are mainly eggs, cow's milk, peanuts and other nuts, fish and seafood, soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame. You don't need to introduce "all" of them one by one, but it is advisable to do so individually and observe the baby with these high-risk groups.
AllergenicFoods.dairy: Cow's milk dairy: milk, yogurt, cheese, standard formulas (the most frequent allergy in infants).
AllergenicFoods.nuts: Peanuts and nuts: walnut, almond, hazelnut, pistachio, cashew, etc.
AllergenicFoods.gluten: Gluten cereals: wheat, barley, rye; also oats in some cases.
